common_name: Abunda Giant White Bacopa (Large-Flowered Vigorous Trailing Bacopa)

planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Abunda Giant White was bred for noticeably larger flowers and a more vigorous trailing habit than standard bacopa cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, keeping soil consistently moist since bacopa wilts quickly if allowed to dry out. Abunda Giant White produces a dense, vigorously trailing mound of small, dark green leaves covered in white, five-petaled flowers noticeably larger than those of standard bacopa cultivars, giving the plant a fuller, showier look in a hanging basket or container spiller role. Its extra vigor lets it fill out a large basket faster than older, more compact bacopa selections. Regular fertilizing supports its continuous bloom, and a partly shaded site in the hottest part of the day helps it perform its best through a Gulf South summer.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, keeping soil consistently moist since bacopa wilts quickly if allowed to dry out. Pink Bacopa produces a dense, trailing mound of small, dark green leaves smothered in tiny, soft pink, five-petaled flowers nearly all season, offering a gentler color option than the more commonly available white and blue bacopa cultivars for a mixed hanging basket or container planting. Regular fertilizing supports its continuous bloom, and a partly shaded site in the hottest part of the day helps it perform its best through a Gulf South summer.

common_name: Butterfly White Pentas (Heat-Proof White Star-Cluster Pollinator Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Butterfly White is a Pentas lanceolata cultivar in the heat-tolerant, compact Butterfly series.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Butterfly White produces dense, rounded clusters of tubular, star-shaped white flowers throughout the warm season, a clean, neutral color that combines easily with the brighter reds, pinks, and lavenders of its Butterfly series siblings in a mixed pollinator planting. Pentas is one of the most valuable warm-season annuals for Gulf South butterfly and hummingbird gardens, its flower clusters providing a concentrated nectar resource attracting monarchs, gulf fritillaries, sulphurs, hummingbirds, and many other pollinators through the long Gulf South summer. It blooms without pause from planting through frost in zone 9, maintaining vigorous flower production through the hottest part of summer that stalls many other bedding annuals. In zone 10-12 it grows as a perennial subshrub; in zone 9 it is a warm-season annual that may self-sow in sheltered, mild winters.
